chapter_theme: The lament for the past (இறந்தகாலத்திரங்கல்): fourteen couplets in which Pattinathar counts the ways he was ruined, by preaching sastras to the unfit, by wealth and influence, by greed for land and gold, by the company of fools and of the blind who had no guru, by taking wives, children and the corpse-smelling body for real, by praise, and even by faultless Siva-worship through countless births that did not free him. The last four turn the refrain from 'I was ruined' to 'I died', with the body named as its own enemy.
structure_note: Each couplet ends கெட்டேனே (I was ruined), and in 625, 627, 629, 630 and 632 the fuller பதியிழந்து கெட்டேனே (I lost the Lord and was ruined). 633 to 635 end மாண்டேனே (I died), and 633 alone has the third person மாண்டானே; 636 returns to கெட்டேனே.

623.reading: I expounded the sastras, which are mean words to men who have no skill in the word, and lost my own cleverness and was ruined.
623.nuance: Two readings of புன்சொல்: the sastras are poor words when given to men unable to take them, or the sastras themselves are poor words. சதுர் is skill or wit; the teacher lost what he set out to give.

624.reading: As my influence grew and grew, a new delusion came upon me; I stumbled and walked head downward and was ruined.
624.nuance: செல்வாக்கு is standing or influence rather than wealth as such; தலைகீழாய் நடந்து (walking upside down) is the picture of a life inverted by it.

625.reading: In the usual places of the world and in desire for land and gold, never slackening in habit, I lost the Lord and was ruined.
625.nuance: பதி is the Lord (Pati) and also a town or home; the refrain பதியிழந்து reads as losing the Lord and as losing one's place. தலிராமல் is read as தளராமல், not slackening.

626.reading: Saying 'all this rare earth, pegged with its boundary stakes, is our holding', I talked big and was ruined.
626.nuance: காணி is a land-holding; ஆணி the stake that marks it. The boast is of ownership of what is only staked out.

627.reading: Joining fools who had no conduct and talking pretence with them, I lost the Lord and was ruined.
627.nuance: பாசாங்கு is show or hypocrisy; the ruin is company and the speech it breeds, not any single deed.

628.reading: Joining the blind who had no guru's path, I lost my mind inside the path of the womb and was ruined.
628.nuance: குரு and குருடர் (the blind) play on each other. கருமார்க்கம் is the path of the womb (கரு), rebirth, or the path of action (கருமம், karma); both readings fit a verse that opposes the guru's way to it.

629.reading: Not thinking of the greatness of Hara who drank the poison, I took children and wives for real, lost the Lord and was ruined.
629.nuance: மெய் என்று, taking them as true or lasting, is the fault, not having them.

630.reading: Taking the great body that already smells of the corpse for real, through greed for money I lost the Lord and was ruined.
630.nuance: பிணவாசம் உற்ற, having the smell of a corpse, is said of the living body; the money-lust serves a body that is already dead.

631.reading: While the poets who saw me praised me heavily, the well-fed body puffed itself up and I was ruined.
631.nuance: உப்பரித்து, swelling, is of the body and the pride together; the praise is bought by feeding poets.

632.reading: Taking countless births I performed the worship of Siva and still did not escape; I lost the Lord and was ruined.
632.nuance: பிழையாமல் is 'without fault' or 'without escaping'; the first gives worship done faultlessly for countless lives that still lost the Lord, the second the same conclusion stated. Either way ritual worship repeated through births is what failed.

633.reading: The body that cannot bear even the touch of a small ant he handed over to be bound and burned, and he died.
633.nuance: The one verse in the third person; the man who shielded the body from an ant consents at the end to its tying and cremation. உறுக்க may also be 'to be reviled'.

634.reading: Without the sense to think that one's own body is one's own enemy, I took it for joy and died.

635.reading: Skin, bone and flesh, and bones beside them grown on old rice: calling such bodies my kin, I swaggered and died.
635.nuance: மேல் எலும்பு, the other bones, are read as the bodies of relatives: kinship is one set of fed bones claiming another.

636.reading: With no dealings coming my way and no wealth coming in, I spoke wasted words, my mind churned, and I was ruined.
636.nuance: போக்குவரத்து is traffic or dealings and பொருள்வரத்து income; the verse may describe the poverty that followed ruin, or the anxiety of waiting for custom that never came. வாக்கழிவு, waste of speech, is idle or ruinous talk.

links.note: The Naladiyar's petty-minded say 'we are rich' and never think where they must go, and their wealth vanishes like lightning; Pattinathar's boast 'all this earth is our holding' is the same speech, confessed in the first person after the vanishing.

Sivavakkiyar calls children, wives and kin maya and asks whether they can come along when Death calls; Pattinathar says he took children and wives for real and lost the Lord. Both make the error one of taking them as true rather than of having them.
Sivavakkiyar's fine body stinks when the Arbiter calls and is carried only as far as the cremation keeper; Pattinathar's body already has the corpse-smell while he chases money for it.

Sivavakkiyar asks how many flowers he threw, mantras he recited and temples he circled in vain; Pattinathar says he performed Siva's worship through countless births and lost the Lord. Both renounce the ritual path from inside it, having done it.

Tirumular says release comes with joy to worshippers who offer food, lamps and incense and think on him in love; Pattinathar says Siva-worship through countless births did not free him. The conflict holds if Pattinathar's பூசை is the same offering-worship Tirumular commends; it dissolves if Tirumular's condition, love and thought, is what Pattinathar lacked.

The Naladiyar asks what it matters whether the body is dragged with a rope or buried once the dancer has left it; Pattinathar's man who could not bear an ant on his body consents at death to its binding and burning. The body that was everything becomes a thing one lets others dispose of.

The Kural says that for those bent on ending births even the body is excess; Pattinathar says the body is one's own enemy and he died not knowing it. The Kural states the ascetic's view, Pattinathar the cost of not holding it.

source_issues: 633 ends மாண்டானே (he died) where the neighbouring units 634 and 635 end மாண்டேனே (I died); either the third person is deliberate or the vowel sign has dropped.
625 தலிராமல் is read as தளராமல்; the printed form is not a word.
